title: Release IO stability gate and onboarding checklist for locked model versions
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Define a deterministic, machine-verifiable IO surface and performance-profile publishing process that acts as a release gate for any model version that customers can 'lock' (release-level versions). This ticket produces: 1) an onboarding checklist for model owners, 2) a machine-readable IO contract schema (prompt shapes, required/optional fields, parameter ranges, structured output versioning), 3) a performance profile spec and publication path, and 4) the test harness and gating rules integrated into the model registry + CI pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable manifest schema is specified (manifest v1) and validated by a schema file in infra-repo: manifest_schema_v1.json
Onboarding checklist published in Confluence with sign-off steps for Research/Applied ML, Infra, and Product
Compatibility test harness merged (tests/run_onboarding_compat.py) that validates prompt shapes, sample inputs, and canonical outputs for a provided seed prompt set

Performance profile publishing implemented: model manifests must include p50/p95/p99 latencies for example seq lengths, throughput (tokens/s per GPU), memory footprint, and recommended quantization profile
CI gate blocks publish of a model manifest without a passing 'stable-io' tag and signed manifest file
Developer docs and Console UI card for 'Stable IO' visible in model catalog with link to the manifest and human-readable summary
rollout_plan: Draft schema and checklist -> internal review (2 days)
Implement schema validation in model-registry CI (3 days)
Create compatibility test harness and add to runtime-test pipeline (4 days)
Publish docs and sample manifests -> internal trial with 3 existing pinned models (1 week)
Enable CI gate on staging and run full regression; if green, flip gate for newly added model versions only
Monitor console metrics for one week; rollback plan: revert CI gate and remove 'stable-io' enforcement if >5 customer-facing regressions
compatibility_matrix_summary: Prompt shape: supported surfaces = {single-string completion, structured chat turns, tool-calling envelope}; all must declare 'schema_version' and 'primary_input_key'

Output shape: two declared forms: free-text and strict-json. Strict-json must include 'schema_version', 'payload', and 'diagnostics' keys. Any change to 'payload' shape requires a new manifest major version

Parameters: default sampling parameters must be declared in manifest. Runtime clamps are allowed but only to narrower ranges (e.g., temperature runtime override allowed in [0,1] if manifest declares [0,2])
Unknown fields: runtime must ignore unknown input keys but surface a normalized warning in diagnostics if present
Function/tool calling: signature stability required; optional fields must be tagged 'nullable' in manifest. Removal of required arguments is a breaking change
performance_profile_schema: Required fields for published profile: seq_lengths (list), p50_latency_ms (list), p95_latency_ms (list), p99_latency_ms (list), throughput_tps_per_gpu (list), memory_gpu_mb (list), recommended_batch_sizes (list), quant_profile_id (string)
Profiles must include the hardware spec used (GPU model, driver, framework version) and the warmup steps and sampling mode used to capture numbers
We publish two view layers: machine-readable JSON attached to manifest and human summary card in Console with normalized score and cost estimate per 1k tokens
Profiles for quantized variants must reference the parent model id and quantization tag; fallback logic documented in manifest
